technical_and_design_decisions: Use Spring XD's module extension points to implement custom Kafka encoders and decoders.
Implement the gpfdist sink and gpload tasklet by leveraging Greenplum's external table and parallel loading features.
Integrate Flo and admin_ui using a modern frontend build pipeline and REST API endpoints provided by Spring XD.
Implement dynamic classpath support using custom URLClassLoaders to isolate module dependencies and support property-based classpath resolution.
Decouple Hadoop dependencies by moving them out of the root classloader and into module-specific classloaders.
assumptions: The development environment, CI/CD pipeline, and base Spring XD project are already set up.
Access to a GPDB/HAWQ instance and a Kafka cluster is available for testing.
The team has sufficient knowledge of Spring XD internals, Spring Batch, and Kafka.
One workday equals 8 hours of focused development effort.
Effort estimates cover design, implementation, unit testing, and basic integration testing for each activity.

activities.activity_description: Implement the ability to customize encoders and decoders used by the Kafka source, sink, and bus modules (U1).
Create an out-of-the-box gpfdist sink module to enable ultra-fast data movement from various sources into GPDB/HAWQ (U2).
Set up UI infrastructure to integrate admin_ui and Flo for managing and visualizing Spring XD streams and jobs (U3).
Create an end-to-end Kafka use-case to study, demonstrate, and verify Kafka + XD play built for scale and performance (U4).
Implement an efficient approach to read files using a tasklet approach rather than reading line-by-line and keeping it in-memory (U5).
Create a gpload tasklet to ingest data from various sources into GPDB in an efficient manner (U6).

activities.activity_name: Remove Hadoop Dependencies from Root Classpath
activities.activity_description: Remove Hadoop dependencies from the root classpath to avoid classloading penalties at startup and decouple for non-HDFS scenarios (U7).
Add support for dynamic classpath for modules, allowing flexibility to load dependencies based on module options or specific locations (U8).
Perform end-to-end integration testing of all new features and update relevant documentation.
